svg.title: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not around it: Renovate validates through its pinned download without a global installation
svg.text: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not around
Scenario: Renovate validates through its pinned download without a global installation

g.text: Then a project without Renovate installed gets the pinned validator, which refuses an
unknown option and accepts the generated configuration
One terminal session in a freshly generated project, on a machine with no Renovate installed. The developer writes an
option Renovate does not know into the configuration.
task renovate:validate installs the Renovate release the project pins into a fresh folder, and its first line names that
release. It answers "Invalid configuration option: unknownOptionForTest" and fails with exit status 1. Once git puts the
generated configuration back, the same task answers "Config validated successfully against 1 file(s)".
And when the npm registry cannot be reached, the task says the configuration was not
checked, and the retry validates it once the registry answers
Same project, now with npm pointed at a registry that does not exist, http://registry.invalid/, and an empty npm cache.
Renovate cannot be downloaded. The task says "could not be downloaded, so the configuration was NOT checked" and fails
with exit status 2, where a refused configuration fails with exit status 1.
The second run is the retry that message asks for. The registry answers again, and the same task answers "Config
validated successfully against 1 file(s)".
And the task ignores a damaged copy that npx left in npm's cache and validates with a
freshly checked copy
This card gets its own home folder, so the damage stays in it. npx runs the pinned Renovate once, and npm keeps the
unpacked files in its cache, under ~/.npm/_npx. Then truncate cuts the validator's main file down to 200 bytes, as wc
shows.
npx would run that broken file the next time, and its crash would read like a refused configuration. task
renovate:validate does not touch it. npm unpacks Renovate into a fresh folder and checks every package against the
checksum the registry publishes, then the task checks the version. It answers "Config validated successfully against 1
file(s)".
